chunks: As for what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar:
He said: I asked Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him): 'Can I make up the daytime salat at night during travel?' He said to him: 'Yes.'
Isma'il ibn Jabir said: 'Can I make up the daytime salat at night during travel?' He said: 'No.'
He (Isma'il) said: 'But you said yes!' He (the Imam) said: 'That one is capable, and you are not capable.'

key_terms.أَقْضِي: qada' (making up): performing a missed voluntary act of worship after its designated time
key_terms.صَلَاةَ النَّهَارِ: daytime salat: here specifically the daytime nawafil (supererogatory prayers), not the obligatory prayers, as established by the chapter heading
key_terms.يُطِيقُ: is capable (yutiq): possesses the physical and devotional capacity for this additional act; the operative condition determining the ruling

ai.seo_question: Can missed daytime nawafil prayers be made up at night during travel according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS)?
ai.summary: This hadith records Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) giving apparently contradictory rulings to two companions regarding the qada' of daytime nawafil at night during travel. Placed by Shaykh Tusi in al-Istibsar to reconcile conflicting narrations, the Imam resolves the apparent contradiction by revealing that the permission is conditioned on individual capacity: Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar possesses the requisite devotional and physical ability, while Isma'il ibn Jabir does not. This establishes a key jurisprudential principle that certain supererogatory permissions are subject to personal capability (taqah).
